lines.text: Some problems contain smaller copies of themselves. Recursion solves them with a procedure that calls itself — one of the most beautiful ideas in computer science.
A tree is a trunk with two smaller trees on top.
A countdown from 5 is “say 5, then count down from 4”.
The problem contains a smaller version of itself.
Every recursive procedure needs a base case: a simple situation where it stops calling itself.
Without one it would never end.
The recursive case calls the procedure again with a SMALLER input, so it gets closer to the base case each time.
Draw a branch, then two smaller branches at angles, each drawing two smaller branches… until the branches are tiny.
The same recursive function in Python: a base case and a recursive call with a smaller number.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
